what_its_for: Tenapanor is used to treat irritable bowel syndrome with constipation (IBS-C) in adults. It works by reducing the amount of sodium absorbed in your intestines, which pulls more water into your gut to help soften stools and make them easier to pass. It also helps reduce belly pain and discomfort that comes with IBS-C.
how_to_take: Take tenapanor by mouth twice a day, immediately BEFORE your morning and evening meals. Swallow the tablet whole. Do not crush, chew, or split the tablet. Try to take it at the same times every day to help you remember. Do not take it on an empty stomach or after eating — timing with meals is very important for this medicine to work properly and to reduce side effects.
dosing: The usual adult dose is 50 mg taken twice daily (once before breakfast and once before dinner). Always follow the dose your doctor prescribed. Do not take more or less than directed.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at your regular scheduled time before your next meal. Do NOT take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. Just continue with your regular schedule.
storage: Store tenapanor at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep the tablets in the original bottle with the cap tightly closed. Protect it from moisture — do NOT store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. IMPORTANT: This medicine can cause serious harm to young children. Store it in a secure place away from children at all times.
what_to_avoid: Avoid giving this medicine to children under 18 years old — it is only approved for adults. Avoid taking it after meals or on an empty stomach, as this increases the risk of diarrhea. Be cautious if you are also taking other medications that affect the gut or water balance — talk to your pharmacist or doctor about all your medicines, vitamins, and supplements.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: severe or worsening diarrhea that does not go away, signs of dehydration such as dizziness, lightheadedness, decreased urination, or feeling very thirsty, bloody stools, severe stomach pain or cramping, or any allergic reaction such as rash, hives, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing. Also call your doctor if you feel the medicine is not working after a few weeks.
when_it_works: You may start to notice improvement in your bowel movements and belly pain within the first 1 to 2 weeks of taking tenapanor. However, it may take up to 4 weeks to feel the full benefit. Keep taking it as directed even if you do not feel better right away. Do not stop without talking to your doctor.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Very little of this drug is absorbed into the bloodstream, but talk to your doctor before using it during pregnancy or while nursing. Children: Tenapanor should NOT be used in children under 18 years old. It can cause severe diarrhea and dangerous fluid loss in young children. Older adults: No dose adjustment is typically needed for older adults, but let your doctor know if you have kidney or liver problems. Kidney or liver disease: Tenapanor is not significantly absorbed into the bloodstream, so dose changes are generally not required, but always inform your doctor of any health conditions you have.
